chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Does madhy invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: No, and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it; rather, it is like saliva and mucus.

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: the garment or clothing affected by the substance
key_terms.الْبُزَاقِ: saliva, used here as a comparison
key_terms.الْجَسَدُ: the body in relation to ritual cleanliness
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُخَاطِ: mucus, used here as a comparison
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: ritual ablution required for acts such as salat
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: is washed; indicating whether purification is required

ai.seo_question: Does madhy invalidate wudu (ablution) or require washing the body and clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on madhy, stating that it does not invalidate wudu (ablution) and does not require washing from the garment or body. The Imam عليه السلام classifies it as analogous to saliva and mucus, indicating ritual non-impurity in this context.
